props.title: Whatever It Takes

sections.content: Whatever It Takes belongs to the wave of teen romantic comedies that flooded theaters in the late 1990s and early 2000s, following the massive success of She's All That (1999). Like 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) and Drive Me Crazy (1999), it loosely adapts a classic literary work - in this case, Cyrano de Bergerac - into a modern high school setting. The film stars James Franco and Shane West as two friends who help each other pursue their respective crushes through elaborate schemes, only to realize they've been chasing the wrong people all along.

sections.content: The film marked one of James Franco's earliest roles, coming just before his breakout in Freaks and Geeks (1999). While Whatever It Takes follows many familiar teen movie tropes established by Clueless (1995), it stands out for its gender-flipped take on Cyrano, with both male leads manipulating their way through romantic entanglements. The movie fits perfectly within the era's obsession with modernizing classic literature for teen audiences, alongside films like Get Over It (2001) and O (2001).

The early 2000s teen movie boom was marked by increasingly self-aware entries like Not Another Teen Movie (2001), which directly parodied many of the tropes seen in Whatever It Takes. This era of teen films often featured future stars in early roles - just as Franco appeared here, Can't Hardly Wait (1998) featured early performances from Jason Segel and Selma Blair, while American Pie (1999) launched several careers. sections.content: While Whatever It Takes didn't achieve the cultural impact of contemporaries like American Pie (1999) or Bring It On (2000), it represents a crucial moment in teen cinema when the genre began incorporating more complex romantic plots beyond simple makeover narratives. This shift continued through films like Save the Last Dance (2001) and A Cinderella Story (2004), though few maintained the direct literary connections of the late 90s wave.
